Integrating structural neuroimaging, cognitive assessments, and multi-omic profiles requires latent representations that remain both clinically predictive and anatomically or molecularly localizable. Classical linear factorizations such as principal component analysis and canonical correlation analysis disperse biological variance across dense, sign-mixed combinations of features, whereas end-to-end deep neural networks obscure how individual brain regions or genes drive patient-level predictions. We present the Similarity-driven Multi-view Representation (SiMR) framework (`pysimlr v0.43.1`), which couples a sparse, non-negative, approximately orthogonal linear input projection (`nsa_flow`) with interchangeable linear (Similarity-driven Multi-view Linear Representation, `SiMLR`), non-linear decoder (Linear Entrypoint with Non-linear Decoders, `LEND`), and invertible normalizing-flow (Normalizing-Flow SiMR, `Flow-SiMR-V`) alignment modules. Across `{python} N.n_blocks` benchmarks spanning six multi-view biomedical cohorts and six synthetic ground-truth regimes, we evaluate `{python} N.n_models_word` candidate architectures across linear subspace probes, axis-aligned tree probes, and feature-support recovery. In the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative Mild Cognitive Impairment (`ADNI-MCI`, $N = 1,084$) cohort, aligning baseline regional brain volumes, volume-to-surface-area ratios, and Diffeomorphic Registration-based Cortical Thickness (`DiReCT`) with 11 neuropsychological scales during training improves out-of-sample composite cognitive prediction from structural magnetic resonance imaging alone from $R^2 =$ `{python} N.adni_pca` (principal component analysis) to $R^2 =$ `{python} N.adni_best_r2` (`{python} N.adni_best_model`). Across `{python} N.attr_n_halves` separate half-sample refits of `ADNI-MCI`, the predictive component isolates entorhinal, temporal, and inferior parietal regions that replicate across subsamples. Evaluating learned representations across multi-variable linear probes and single-axis decision trees demonstrates that while linear regression is algebraically invariant to post-hoc column mixing, coordinate-aligned SiMR projections preserve `{python} N.adni_rf_ratio`-fold higher single-factor predictive utility on `ADNI-MCI` ($R^2 =$ `{python} N.adni_rf_best` for `{python} N.adni_rf_best_model` versus `{python} N.adni_pca_rf` for principal component analysis), and recover ground-truth feature supports with $F_1$ between `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_min` and `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_max` at $50\%$ feature sparsity (`q = 0.5`). To resolve shrinkage-sparsity cancellation, simplex distortion, and multi-component collapse in high-dimensional cohorts, `pysimlr v0.43.1` introduces non-subtractive quantile sparsification (`sparseness_type="hard"`), exact radial simplex normalization, two-stage support-restricted uniform shrinkage (`fit_uniform_shrunk`) with rank-aware directional defaults (`resolve_directional_defaults`), calibrated out-of-bag intraclass correlation (`ICC(1)`) stability (`latent_stability`), ensemble bagging (`bagged_fit`), and permutation or Gaussian maximum-likelihood path inference (`path_model`, `observed_path_model`). Across `{python} N.syn_n_seeds`-seed synthetic theorem checks and `{python} N.v043_n_fits` plus `{python} N.us_n_fits` real-data revisit fits, removing subtractive shrinkage cancellation and enforcing disjoint column supports maintains exact column orthogonality while preserving single-axis predictive utility. Multi-variable linear accuracy measures subspace capacity alone; evaluating coordinate-level localization requires axis-sensitive probes, non-subtractive constraints, and out-of-bag stability checks matched to the geometry of the objective.
